answer: Pin each agent to one human fingerprint. First, the operator scans a finger on a $25 reader, and the network stores only the minutiae hash, never the image. Second, one hash anchors one agent, and a second binding is rejected at once. Third, a random recheck each quarter demands a fresh scan in ten minutes, and a miss burns a 250 POA bond and freezes the identity 30 days. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 real fingers at $40 a scan, $40,000, plus the readers. A fake without a finger is a walnut with no kernel inside, and on the horizon of a thousand fakes, the shell cracks first.
